question: Should exact requester adoption of descendant output count as terminal descendant delivery even when the requester's later outward send fails?
rationale: That choice determines whether retry suppression is correct product semantics or whether the completion must remain pending for a durable inbox or outbox path; tests cannot choose the boundary.

options.title: Accept after proof
options.body: Treat narrowly matched requester consumption as terminal delivery after real failed-send and restart proof confirms only consumed descendants stop retrying.

options.title: Require outward delivery
options.body: Keep descendants retryable until the requester result is visibly delivered, moving this accounting into the final send-success boundary.

options.title: Fold into durable inbox
options.body: Pause this patch and solve consumed and unconsumed completion survival together in the broader durable completion inbox design.

recommendation.title: Accept after proof
recommendation.body: Treat narrowly matched requester consumption as terminal delivery after real failed-send and restart proof confirms only consumed descendants stop retrying.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history spans the cron, lifecycle, and SQLite decision surfaces affected by the terminal-delivery boundary.
